Engineering for Equity面向公平的工程

Chapter 4. Engineering for Equity · 第 4 章 · 面向公平的工程

Written by Demma Rodriguez; Edited by Riona MacNamara.

作者：Demma Rodriguez；编辑：Riona MacNamara。

In earlier chapters, we’ve explored the contrast between programming as the production of code that addresses the problem of the moment, and software engineering as the broader application of code, tools, policies, and processes to a dynamic and ambiguous problem that can span decades or even lifetimes. In this chapter, we’ll discuss the unique responsibilities of an engineer when designing products for a broad base of users. Further, we evaluate how an organization, by embracing diversity, can design systems that work for everyone, and avoid perpetuating harm against our users.

在前面几章里，我们探讨了一种对比：编程是产出代码、解决当下的问题；而软件工程则是把代码、工具、政策与流程更广泛地应用于一个动态而模糊、可能跨越数十年甚至一生的问题。在本章，我们将讨论工程师在为广大用户群设计产品时所肩负的独特责任。进一步地，我们会评估：一个组织如何通过拥抱多样性，设计出对所有人都奏效的系统，并避免对我们的用户持续造成伤害。

As new as the field of software engineering is, we’re newer still at understanding the impact it has on underrepresented people and diverse societies. We did not write this chapter because we know all the answers. We do not. In fact, understanding how to engineer products that empower and respect all our users is still something Google is learning to do. We have had many public failures in protecting our most vulnerable users, and so we are writing this chapter because the path forward to more equitable products begins with evaluating our own failures and encouraging growth.

软件工程这个领域固然年轻，而我们对它如何影响代表性不足的人群与多元社会的理解，就更年轻了。我们写这一章，并不是因为我们知道所有答案。我们并不知道。事实上，如何以工程手段打造赋能并尊重所有用户的产品，Google 自己仍在学习。我们在保护最脆弱用户方面有过许多公开的失败；我们之所以写这一章，是因为通往更公平产品的道路，始于审视我们自己的失败、并鼓励成长。

We are also writing this chapter because of the increasing imbalance of power between those who make development decisions that impact the world and those who simply must accept and live with those decisions that sometimes disadvantage already marginalized communities globally. It is important to share and reflect on what we’ve learned so far with the next generation of software engineers. It is even more important that we help influence the next generation of engineers to be better than we are today.

我们写这一章，还因为另一个日益失衡的权力格局：一边是做出影响世界的开发决策的人，另一边是只能接受并忍受这些决策的人——而这些决策有时会让全球本已边缘化的群体处境更不利。把我们迄今学到的东西分享、反思给下一代软件工程师，很重要。而更重要的是，帮助影响下一代工程师，让他们比我们今天做得更好。

原书第 97 页

Just picking up this book means that you likely aspire to be an exceptional engineer. You want to solve problems. You aspire to build products that drive positive outcomes for the broadest base of people, including people who are the most difficult to reach. To do this, you will need to consider how the tools you build will be leveraged to change the trajectory of humanity, hopefully for the better.

拿起这本书，大概说明你有志成为一名杰出的工程师。你想解决问题。你渴望打造能为最广泛人群——包括最难触达的人群——带来积极结果的产品。要做到这一点，你需要思考：你所构建的工具将被如何用来改变人类的轨迹，但愿是向好的方向。

Bias Is the Default · 偏见是默认状态

When engineers do not focus on users of different nationalities, ethnicities, races, genders, ages, socioeconomic statuses, abilities, and belief systems, even the most talented staff will inadvertently fail their users. Such failures are often unintentional; all people have certain biases, and social scientists have recognized over the past several decades that most people exhibit unconscious bias, enforcing and promulgating existing stereotypes. Unconscious bias is insidious and often more difficult to mitigate than intentional acts of exclusion. Even when we want to do the right thing, we might not recognize our own biases. By the same token, our organizations must also recognize that such bias exists and work to address it in their workforces, product development, and user outreach.

当工程师不关注不同国籍、族裔、种族、性别、年龄、社会经济地位、能力与信仰体系的用户时，即便最有才华的员工也会在不经意间辜负他们的用户。这类失败往往是无意的；人人都有某种偏见，而社会科学家在过去几十年里已经认识到：大多数人都会表现出无意识偏见，强化并传播既有的刻板印象。无意识偏见是隐蔽的，往往比有意的排斥行为更难缓解。即便我们想做正确的事，也可能认不出自己的偏见。同样，我们的组织也必须认识到这种偏见的存在，并努力在员工队伍、产品开发与用户拓展中应对它。

Because of bias, Google has at times failed to represent users equitably within their products, with launches over the past several years that did not focus enough on underrepresented groups. Many users attribute our lack of awareness in these cases to the fact that our engineering population is mostly male, mostly White or Asian, and certainly not representative of all the communities that use our products. The lack of representation of such users in our workforce means that we often do not have the requisite diversity to understand how the use of our products can affect underrepresented or vulnerable users.

由于偏见，Google 有时未能在产品中公平地代表用户——过去几年里的一些发布，没有对代表性不足的群体给予足够关注。许多用户把我们在这些案例中的意识不足，归因于我们的工程师队伍主要是男性、主要是白人或亚裔，当然也不能代表使用我们产品的所有社群。员工队伍中这类用户代表不足，意味着我们常常缺乏必要的多样性，去理解我们产品的使用会如何影响代表性不足或脆弱的用户。

Case study: Google Misses the Mark on Racial Inclusion. In 2015, software engineer Jacky Alciné pointed out that the image recognition algorithms in Google Photos were classifying his black friends as “gorillas.” Google was slow to respond to these mistakes and incomplete in addressing them. What caused such a monumental failure?

案例研究：Google 在种族包容上失手。2015 年，软件工程师 Jacky Alciné 指出，Google 相册的图像识别算法把他的黑人朋友归类为“大猩猩”。Google 对这些错误反应迟缓、处理也不彻底。是什么导致了如此惨痛的失败？

  • Image recognition algorithms depend on being supplied a “proper” (often meaning “complete”) dataset. The photo data fed into Google’s image recognition algorithm was clearly incomplete. In short, the data did not represent the population.

    图像识别算法依赖于被供给一份“恰当”（往往意味着“完整”）的数据集。喂给 Google 图像识别算法的照片数据显然是不完整的。简而言之，数据没有代表整个人群。

原书第 98 页

  • Google itself (and the tech industry in general) did not (and does not) have much black representation, and that affects decisions subjective in the design of such algorithms and the collection of such datasets. The unconscious bias of the organization itself likely led to a more representative product being left on the table.

    Google 自身（以及整个科技行业）当时（和现在）都没有多少黑人代表，这影响了此类算法设计与此类数据集收集中那些带有主观性的决策。组织自身的无意识偏见，很可能让一个更具代表性的产品被白白放过。

  • Google’s target market for image recognition did not adequately include such underrepresented groups. Google’s tests did not catch these mistakes; as a result, our users did, which both embarrassed Google and harmed our users. As late as 2018, Google still had not adequately addressed the underlying problem.

    Google 图像识别的目标市场没有充分纳入这些代表性不足的群体。Google 的测试没有逮住这些错误；结果是我们的用户逮住了，这既让 Google 难堪，也伤害了我们的用户。直到 2018 年，Google 仍未充分解决这一根本问题。

In this example, our product was inadequately designed and executed, failing to properly consider all racial groups, and as a result, failed our users and caused Google bad press. Other technology suffers from similar failures: autocomplete can return offensive or racist results. Google’s Ad system could be manipulated to show racist or offensive ads. YouTube might not catch hate speech, though it is technically outlawed on that platform.

在这个例子里，我们的产品设计与执行都不充分，没能恰当考虑所有种族群体，结果辜负了用户、也让 Google 蒙受差评。其他技术也遭受类似失败：自动补全会返回冒犯性或种族主义的结果；Google 的广告系统可能被操纵来展示种族主义或冒犯性广告；YouTube 也许逮不住仇恨言论，尽管该平台在技术上禁止它。

In all of these cases, the technology itself is not really to blame. Autocomplete, for example, was not designed to target users or to discriminate. But it was also not resilient enough in its design to exclude discriminatory language that is considered hate speech. As a result, the algorithm returned results that caused harm to our users. The harm to Google itself should also be obvious: reduced user trust and engagement with the company. For example, Black, Latinx, and Jewish applicants could lose faith in Google as a platform or even as an inclusive environment itself, therefore undermining Google’s goal of improving representation in hiring.

在所有这些案例里，技术本身其实并非真正的罪魁。例如，自动补全在设计时并不是为了针对用户或歧视。但它在设计上也不够强健，无法排除那些被视为仇恨言论的歧视性语言。结果，算法返回了伤害用户的结果。对 Google 自身的损害也应当是显而易见的：用户对公司的信任与参与度下降。例如，黑人、拉丁裔和犹太裔求职者可能会失去对 Google 作为一个平台、甚至作为一个包容环境本身的信心，从而损害 Google 在招聘中提升代表性的目标。

How could this happen? After all, Google hires technologists with impeccable education and/or professional experience—exceptional programmers who write the best code and test their work. “Build for everyone” is a Google brand statement, but the truth is that we still have a long way to go before we can claim that we do. One way to address these problems is to help the software engineering organization itself look like the populations for whom we build products.

这怎么可能发生？毕竟，Google 雇用的技术人员都拥有无可挑剔的教育背景和/或职业经验——都是写出最好代码、并测试自己工作的杰出程序员。“为每个人而建（Build for everyone）”是 Google 的品牌宣言，但事实是，距离我们能真正宣称做到这一点，还有很长的路要走。解决这些问题的一个办法，是让软件工程组织本身看起来就像我们为之造产品的那些人群。

原书第 99 页

Understanding the Need for Diversity · 理解多样性的必要性

At Google, we believe that being an exceptional engineer requires that you also focus on bringing diverse perspectives into product design and implementation. It also means that Googlers responsible for hiring or interviewing other engineers must contribute to building a more representative workforce. For example, if you interview other engineers for positions at your company, it is important to learn how biased outcomes happen in hiring. There are significant prerequisites for understanding how to anticipate harm and prevent it. To get to the point where we can build for everyone, we first must understand our representative populations. We need to encourage engineers to have a wider scope of educational training.

在 Google，我们相信：要成为一名杰出工程师，你还必须专注于把多元视角带入产品设计与实现。这也意味着，负责招聘或面试其他工程师的 Googler，必须为建设一支更具代表性的员工队伍出力。例如，如果你在公司面试应聘工程师岗位的人，那么了解带偏见的结果在招聘中是如何产生的，就很重要。要理解如何预见伤害并防止它，有一些重要的先决条件。要达到“能为每个人而建”的地步，我们首先必须理解我们所代表的人群。我们需要鼓励工程师拥有更广泛的教育训练范围。

The first order of business is to disrupt the notion that as a person with a computer science degree and/or work experience, you have all the skills you need to become an exceptional engineer. A computer science degree is often a necessary foundation. However, the degree alone (even when coupled with work experience) will not make you an engineer. It is also important to disrupt the idea that only people with computer science degrees can design and build products. Today, most programmers do have a computer science degree; they are successful at building code, establishing theories of change, and applying methodologies for problem solving. However, as the aforementioned examples demonstrate, this approach is insufficient for inclusive and equitable engineering.

首要之事，是打破这样一种观念：作为一个拥有计算机科学学位和/或工作经验的人，你就具备了成为杰出工程师所需的一切技能。计算机科学学位往往是必要的基础。然而，光有学位（即便加上工作经验）并不会让你成为工程师。同样重要的是打破另一种观念：只有拥有计算机科学学位的人才能设计和构建产品。今天，大多数程序员确实有计算机科学学位；他们在写代码、建立变革理论、应用方法论解决问题方面是成功的。然而，正如前面的例子所表明的那样，这种做法对于包容与公平的工程是不够的。

Engineers should begin by focusing all work within the framing of the complete ecosystem they seek to influence. At minimum, they need to understand the population demographics of their users. Engineers should focus on people who are different than themselves, especially people who might attempt to use their products to cause harm. The most difficult users to consider are those who are disenfranchised by the processes and the environment in which they access technology. To address this challenge, engineering teams need to be representative of their existing and future users. In the absence of diverse representation on engineering teams, individual engineers need to learn how to build for all users.

工程师应当从一开始，就把所有工作放在他们想要影响的完整生态系统这一框架内。至少，他们需要理解用户的人口统计学特征。工程师应当关注与自己不同的人，尤其是那些可能试图利用他们的产品来造成伤害的人。最难考虑到的用户，是那些被获取技术的流程与环境所剥夺权利的人。要应对这一挑战，工程团队需要代表他们现有与未来的用户。在工程团队缺乏多元代表的情况下，单个工程师需要学习如何为所有用户而建。

Building Multicultural Capacity · 建设多元文化能力

One mark of an exceptional engineer is the ability to understand how products can advantage and disadvantage different groups of human beings. Engineers are expected to have technical aptitude, but they should also have the discernment to know when to build something and when not to. Discernment includes building the capacity to identify and reject features or products that drive adverse outcomes. This is a lofty and difficult goal, because there is an enormous amount of individualism that goes into being a high-performing engineer. Yet to succeed, we must extend our

杰出工程师的一个标志，是有能力理解产品如何让不同人群受益或受损。工程师被期望具备技术天赋，但他们也应当具备判断力，知道什么时候该造、什么时候不该造。这种判断力包括培养一种能力：识别并拒斥那些导致负面结果的特性或产品。这是一个崇高而艰难的目标，因为要成为高绩效工程师，其中包含着大量的个人主义。然而要成功，我们就必须把视野从自己的小圈子延伸到下一个十亿用户，或那些可能被我们的产品剥夺权利、落在后面的现有用户。

原书第 100 页

focus beyond our own communities to the next billion users or to current users who might be disenfranchised or left behind by our products.

（接上段：我们必须把关注点从自己的小圈子，延伸到下一个十亿用户，或那些可能被我们的产品剥夺权利、落在后面的现有用户。）

Over time, you might build tools that billions of people use daily—tools that influence how people think about the value of human lives, tools that monitor human activity, and tools that capture and persist sensitive data, such as images of their children and loved ones, as well as other types of sensitive data. As an engineer, you might wield more power than you realize: the power to literally change society. It’s critical that on your journey to becoming an exceptional engineer, you understand the innate responsibility needed to exercise power without causing harm. The first step is to recognize the default state of your bias caused by many societal and educational factors. After you recognize this, you’ll be able to consider the often-forgotten use cases or users who can benefit or be harmed by the products you build.

随着时间推移，你可能会打造出数十亿人每天使用的工具——影响人们如何看待人类生命价值的工具、监控人类活动的工具，以及捕获并持久保存敏感数据的工具，比如他们孩子与亲人的照片，以及其他类型的敏感数据。作为工程师，你掌握的权力可能比你意识到的更大：实实在在改变社会的权力。在你成为杰出工程师的旅程中，至关重要的是理解：行使这种权力而不造成伤害，需要一种内在的责任感。第一步，是认识到由诸多社会与教育因素造成的、你偏见的默认状态。认识到这一点之后，你就能去考虑那些常被遗忘的用例，或那些可能因你所造产品而受益、或受害的用户。

The industry continues to move forward, building new use cases for artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning at an ever-increasing speed. To stay competitive, we drive toward scale and efficacy in building a high-talent engineering and technology workforce. Yet we need to pause and consider the fact that today, some people have the ability to design the future of technology and others do not. We need to understand whether the software systems we build will eliminate the potential for entire populations to experience shared prosperity and provide equal access to technology.

这个行业在不断前进，以越来越快的速度为人工智能（AI）与机器学习构建新用例。为了保持竞争力，我们在打造一支高才干工程与技术队伍时，追求规模与效能。然而我们需要停下来思考这样一个事实：今天，有些人有能力设计技术的未来，另一些人则没有。我们需要理解：我们所构建的软件系统，是否会消除整个人群体验共同繁荣、平等获取技术的可能。

Historically, companies faced with a decision between completing a strategic objective that drives market dominance and revenue and one that potentially slows momentum toward that goal have opted for speed and shareholder value. This tendency is exacerbated by the fact that many companies value individual performance and excellence, yet often fail to effectively drive accountability on product equity across all areas. Focusing on underrepresented users is a clear opportunity to promote equity. To continue to be competitive in the technology sector, we need to learn to engineer for global equity.

从历史上看，当公司面临抉择——一边是完成一个带来市场主导与营收的战略目标，另一边是一个可能拖慢这一势头的目标——时，它们选择了速度与股东价值。许多公司看重个人绩效与卓越，却往往未能在所有领域有效推动产品公平上的问责，这加剧了这种倾向。关注代表性不足的用户，是促进公平的一个明确机会。要在科技行业继续保持竞争力，我们需要学会为全球公平而工程。

Today, we worry when companies design technology to scan, capture, and identify people walking down the street. We worry about privacy and how governments might use this information now and in the future. Yet most technologists do not have the requisite perspective of underrepresented groups to understand the impact of racial variance in facial recognition or to understand how applying AI can drive harmful and inaccurate results. Currently, AI-driven facial-recognition software continues to disadvantage people of color or ethnic minorities. Our research is not comprehensive enough and does not include a wide enough range of different skin tones. We cannot expect the output to be valid if both the training data and those creating the software represent only a small subsection of people. In those cases, we should be willing to delay development in favor of trying to get more complete and accurate data, and a more comprehensive and inclusive product.

今天，当公司设计技术去扫描、捕获并识别走在街上的人时，我们会担忧。我们担忧隐私，担忧政府现在和将来会如何使用这些信息。然而，大多数技术人员并不具备代表性不足群体的必要视角，去理解面部识别中种族差异的影响，也不理解应用 AI 如何会导致有害而不准确的结果。当前，AI 驱动的面部识别软件持续让有色人种或少数族裔处于不利地位。我们的研究不够全面，没有涵盖足够广泛的不同肤色。如果训练数据和创造软件的人都只代表人群中的一小部分，我们就不能指望输出是有效的。在这些情况下，我们应当愿意推迟开发，去努力获得更完整、更准确的数据，以及一个更全面、更包容的产品。

原书第 101 页

Data science itself is challenging for humans to evaluate, however. Even when we do have representation, a training set can still be biased and produce invalid results. A study completed in 2016 found that more than 117 million American adults are in a law enforcement facial recognition database. Due to the disproportionate policing of Black communities and disparate outcomes in arrests, there could be racially biased error rates in utilizing such a database in facial recognition. Although the software is being developed and deployed at ever-increasing rates, the independent testing is not. To correct for this egregious misstep, we need to have the integrity to slow down and ensure that our inputs contain as little bias as possible. Google now offers statistical training within the context of AI to help ensure that datasets are not intrinsically biased.

然而，数据科学本身对人类来说就难以评估。即便我们有了代表性，训练集仍可能有偏、产生无效结果。2016 年完成的一项研究发现，超过 1.17 亿美国成年人被收录在执法面部识别数据库中。由于对黑人社区不成比例的警务执法以及逮捕结果的差异，在面部识别中使用这样一个数据库，可能存在带有种族偏见的错误率。尽管这类软件正以越来越快的速度被开发和部署，独立测试却没有跟上。要纠正这个令人震惊的失误，我们需要有诚意慢下来，确保我们的输入包含尽可能少的偏见。Google 如今在 AI 语境下提供统计学培训，以帮助确保数据集本身不带有内在偏见。

Therefore, shifting the focus of your industry experience to include more comprehensive, multicultural, race and gender studies education is not only your responsibility, but also the responsibility of your employer. Technology companies must ensure that their employees are continually receiving professional development and that this development is comprehensive and multidisciplinary. The requirement is not that one individual take it upon themselves to learn about other cultures or other demographics alone. Change requires that each of us, individually or as leaders of teams, invest in continuous professional development that builds not just our software development and leadership skills, but also our capacity to understand the diverse experiences throughout humanity.

因此，把你的行业经验的关注点转向更全面的多元文化、种族与性别研究教育，不仅是你的责任，也是你雇主的责任。科技公司必须确保其员工持续接受职业发展训练，而且这种训练是全面、多学科的。这一要求并不是说要由某个人独自去了解其他文化或其他人群。改变要求我们每一个人——无论是作为个人还是作为团队领导——投资于持续的职业发展，这种发展不仅要建设我们的软件开发与领导技能，还要建设我们理解全人类多元体验的能力。

Making Diversity Actionable · 让多样性可落地

Systemic equity and fairness are attainable if we are willing to accept that we are all accountable for the systemic discrimination we see in the technology sector. We are accountable for the failures in the system. Deferring or abstracting away personal accountability is ineffective, and depending on your role, it could be irresponsible. It is also irresponsible to fully attribute dynamics at your specific company or within your team to the larger societal issues that contribute to inequity. A favorite line among diversity proponents and detractors alike goes something like this: “We are working hard to fix (insert systemic discrimination topic), but accountability is hard. How do we combat (insert hundreds of years) of historical discrimination?” This line of inquiry is a detour to a more philosophical or academic conversation and away from focused efforts to improve work conditions or outcomes. Part of building multicultural capacity requires a more comprehensive understanding of how systems of inequality in society impact the workplace, especially in the technology sector.

如果我们愿意承认：我们每个人都对自己在科技行业所见的系统性歧视负有责任，那么系统性的公平与正义是可以实现的。我们对系统中的失败负有责任。推诿或把个人责任抽象掉是无效的，而且根据你的角色不同，可能是不负责任的。把你所在公司或团队内部的动态，完全归咎于造成不公的更大社会问题，同样是不负责任的。支持多样性者与反对者都爱说这样一句话：“我们正在努力解决（填入某个系统性歧视话题），但问责很难。我们要如何对抗（填入数百年）的历史歧视？”这种问法是一种绕道，把人引向更哲学或学术的对话，偏离了改善工作条件或结果的聚焦努力。建设多元文化能力，一部分需要更全面地理解社会中的不平等体系如何影响职场——尤其是科技行业。

原书第 102 页

If you are an engineering manager working on hiring more people from underrepresented groups, deferring to the historical impact of discrimination in the world is a useful academic exercise. However, it is critical to move beyond the academic conversation to a focus on quantifiable and actionable steps that you can take to drive equity and fairness. For example, as a hiring software engineer manager, you’re accountable for ensuring that your candidate slates are balanced. Are there women or other underrepresented groups in the pool of candidates’ reviews? After you hire someone, what opportunities for growth have you provided, and is the distribution of opportunities equitable? Every technology lead or software engineering manager has the means to augment equity on their teams. It is important that we acknowledge that, although there are significant systemic challenges, we are all part of the system. It is our problem to fix.

如果你是一位工程经理，正在努力招聘更多来自代表性不足群体的人，那么把一切推给世界上歧视的历史影响，是一种有用的学术练习。然而，关键在于超越学术对话，聚焦于你可以采取的、可量化、可落地的步骤，去推动公平与公正。例如，作为一个负责招聘的软件工程师经理，你有责任确保你的候选人名单是平衡的。在被评审的候选人池里，有女性或其他代表性不足群体吗？在你招了某人之后，你提供了哪些成长机会？这些机会的分配公平吗？每一位技术负责人或软件工程经理都有办法在自己团队里增进公平。重要的是我们要承认：尽管存在重大的系统性挑战，但我们都是这个系统的一部分。这是我们要解决的问题。

Reject Singular Approaches · 拒绝单一化方法

We cannot perpetuate solutions that present a single philosophy or methodology for fixing inequity in the technology sector. Our problems are complex and multifactorial. Therefore, we must disrupt singular approaches to advancing representation in the workplace, even if they are promoted by people we admire or who have institutional power.

我们不能再延续那种“用单一哲学或方法论解决科技行业不公”的方案。我们的问题是复杂、多因素的。因此，我们必须打破那种单一化地推进职场代表性的做法，哪怕这些做法是由我们钦佩的人、或拥有制度权力的人所推行的。

One singular narrative held dear in the technology industry is that lack of representation in the workforce can be addressed solely by fixing the hiring pipelines. Yes, that is a fundamental step, but that is not the immediate issue we need to fix. We need to recognize systemic inequity in progression and retention while simultaneously focusing on more representative hiring and educational disparities across lines of race, gender, and socioeconomic and immigration status, for example.

科技界珍爱着一个单一化叙事：员工队伍中代表性不足的问题，可以单靠修好招聘管道来解决。是的，那是基础性的一步，但那不是我们眼下需要修的问题。我们需要认识到晋升与留任中的系统性不公，同时聚焦于更具代表性的招聘，以及跨种族、性别、社会经济与移民身份线的教育差异——举例来说。

In the technology industry, many people from underrepresented groups are passed over daily for opportunities and advancement. Attrition among Black+ Google employees outpaces attrition from all other groups and confounds progress on representation goals. If we want to drive change and increase representation, we need to evaluate whether we’re creating an ecosystem in which all aspiring engineers and other technology professionals can thrive.

在科技行业，许多来自代表性不足群体的人每天都在机会与晋升上被略过。Google 黑人及以上员工的离职率超过所有其他群体，阻碍了代表性目标的进展。如果我们想推动变革、提升代表性，就需要评估我们是否在创造一个让所有有抱负的工程师与其他技术专业人士都能茁壮成长的生态。

Fully understanding an entire problem space is critical to determining how to fix it. This holds true for everything from a critical data migration to the hiring of a representative workforce. For example, if you are an engineering manager who wants to hire more women, don’t just focus on building a pipeline. Focus on other aspects of the hiring, retention, and progression ecosystem and how inclusive it might or might not be to women. Consider whether your recruiters are demonstrating the ability to identify strong candidates who are women as well as men. If you manage a diverse engineering team, focus on psychological safety and invest in increasing multicultural capacity on the team so that new team members feel welcome.

充分理解整个问题空间，对于决定如何修复它至关重要。这一点从关键数据迁移到招聘一支有代表性的员工队伍，一概适用。例如，如果你是一位想招更多女性的工程经理，不要只盯着建管道。要关注招聘、留任与晋升生态的其他方面，以及它对女性究竟包容还是不包容。想想你的招聘人员是否展现出既能识别优秀男性候选人、也能识别优秀女性候选人的能力。如果你管理着一支多元的工程团队，要聚焦心理安全、投资于提升团队的多元文化能力，让新成员感到受欢迎。

原书第 103 页

A common methodology today is to build for the majority use case first, leaving improvements and features that address edge cases for later. But this approach is flawed; it gives users who are already advantaged in access to technology a head start, which increases inequity. Relegating the consideration of all user groups to the point when design has been nearly completed is to lower the bar of what it means to be an excellent engineer. Instead, by building in inclusive design from the start and raising development standards for development to make tools delightful and accessible for people who struggle to access technology, we enhance the experience for all users. Designing for the user who is least like you is not just wise, it’s a best practice. There are pragmatic and immediate next steps that all technologists, regardless of domain, should consider when developing products that avoid disadvantaging or underrepresenting users. It begins with more comprehensive user-experience research. This research should be done with user groups that are multilingual and multicultural and that span multiple countries, socioeconomic class, abilities, and age ranges. Focus on the most difficult or least represented use case first.

今天一种常见方法论是：先为多数用例而建，把处理边缘情况的改进与特性留到以后。但这种做法是有缺陷的；它让那些在获取技术上本已占优的用户占了先机，从而加剧不公。把对所有用户群体的考虑推迟到设计几乎完成之时，就是在降低“杰出工程师”的门槛。相反，从一开始就植入包容式设计、并提高开发标准，让工具对那些难以获取技术的人来说也令人愉悦、可及，我们就能提升所有用户的体验。为那个最不像你的用户做设计，不仅明智，更是最佳实践。所有技术人员，无论身处哪个领域，在开发那些不使某些用户处于不利或代表性不足地位的产品时，都有一些务实而即时的下一步可考虑。它始于更全面的用户体验研究。这项研究应当与多语言、多文化、跨越多个国家、社会经济阶层、能力与年龄段的用户群体一起开展。先聚焦最困难或最缺乏代表性的用例。

Challenge Established Processes · 挑战既有流程

Challenging yourself to build more equitable systems goes beyond designing more inclusive product specifications. Building equitable systems sometimes means challenging established processes that drive invalid results. Consider a recent case evaluated for equity implications. At Google, several engineering teams worked to build a global hiring requisition system. The system supports both external hiring and internal mobility. The engineers and product managers involved did a great job of listening to the requests of what they considered to be their core user group: recruiters. The recruiters were focused on minimizing wasted time for hiring managers and applicants, and they presented the development team with use cases focused on scale and efficiency for those people. To drive efficiency, the recruiters asked the engineering team to include a feature that would highlight performance ratings—specifically lower ratings—to the hiring manager and recruiter as soon as an internal transfer expressed interest in a job.

挑战自己去建设更公平的系统，不止于设计更包容的产品规格。建设公平的系统，有时意味着挑战那些导致无效结果的既有流程。考虑最近一个被评估公平影响的案例。在 Google，几个工程团队合力构建一个全球招聘申请系统。该系统同时支持外部招聘与内部流动。参与的工程师与产品经理很好地倾听了他们所认为的核心用户群——招聘人员——的需求。招聘人员聚焦于尽量减少招聘经理与申请人的时间浪费，并向开发团队提出了围绕这些人规模与效率的用例。为推动效率，招聘人员要求工程团队加入一个特性：一旦某个内部转岗者对某个职位表达兴趣，就把绩效评分——尤其是较低的评分——突出显示给招聘经理与招聘人员。

On its face, expediting the evaluation process and helping jobseekers save time is a great goal. So where is the potential equity concern? The following equity questions were raised:

从表面上看，加快评估流程、帮求职者节省时间是个好目标。那么潜在的公平问题在哪？人们提出了以下公平方面的疑问：

  • Are developmental assessments a predictive measure of performance?

    发展性评估是对绩效的预测性度量吗？

  • Are the performance assessments being presented to prospective managers free of individual bias?

    呈给未来经理的绩效评估是否免于个人偏见？

  • Are performance assessment scores standardized across organizations?

    绩效评估分数在各组织之间是标准化的吗？

原书第 104 页

If the answer to any of these questions is “no,” presenting performance ratings could still drive inequitable, and therefore invalid, results.

如果这些问题中任何一个的答案是“否”，那么展示绩效评分仍可能导致不公平、因而无效的结果。

When an exceptional engineer questioned whether past performance was in fact predictive of future performance, the reviewing team decided to conduct a thorough review. In the end, it was determined that candidates who had received a poor performance rating were likely to overcome the poor rating if they found a new team. In fact, they were just as likely to receive a satisfactory or exemplary performance rating as candidates who had never received a poor rating. In short, performance ratings are indicative only of how a person is performing in their given role at the time they are being evaluated. Ratings, although an important way to measure performance during a specific period, are not predictive of future performance and should not be used to gauge readiness for a future role or qualify an internal candidate for a different team. (They can, however, be used to evaluate whether an employee is properly or improperly slotted on their current team; therefore, they can provide an opportunity to evaluate how to better support an internal candidate moving forward.) This analysis definitely took up significant project time, but the positive trade-off was a more equitable internal mobility process.

当一位杰出工程师质疑“过去的绩效是否真能预测未来绩效”时，评审团队决定做一次彻底审查。最终结论是：那些曾获得较差绩效评分的候选人，如果换到新团队，很可能克服那个较差评分。事实上，他们获得满意或出色绩效评分的可能性，与从未拿过较差评分的候选人一样。简而言之，绩效评分只表明一个人在被评估当时、在其特定岗位上的表现。评分虽是衡量特定时期绩效的重要方式，却不能预测未来绩效，也不应用来衡量一个人是否胜任未来岗位、或判定内部候选人是否有资格进入另一个团队。（不过，它可以用来评估一名员工在当前团队中是否被放对了位置；因此，它可以提供一个机会，去评估今后如何更好地支持这位内部候选人。）这次分析确实占用了大量项目时间，但正向的权衡是：一个更公平的内部流动流程。

Values Versus Outcomes · 价值与结果

Google has a strong track record of investing in hiring. As the previous example illustrates, we also continually evaluate our processes in order to improve equity and inclusion. More broadly, our core values are based on respect and an unwavering commitment to a diverse and inclusive workforce. Yet, year after year, we have also missed our mark on hiring a representative workforce that reflects our users around the globe. The struggle to improve our equitable outcomes persists despite the policies and programs in place to help support inclusion initiatives and promote excellence in hiring and progression. The failure point is not in the values, intentions, or investments of the company, but rather in the application of those policies at the implementation level.

Google 在招聘投入上有着良好记录。正如前一个例子所示，我们也在持续评估自己的流程，以改善公平与包容。更宏观地，我们的核心价值建立在尊重之上，建立在对一支多元、包容员工队伍的坚定承诺之上。然而年复一年，我们在招聘一支反映全球用户的有代表性员工队伍上，也始终未能达标。尽管已有各种政策与计划来支持包容举措、促进招聘与晋升上的卓越，我们改善公平结果的努力仍在艰难挣扎。失败点不在于公司的价值、意图或投入，而在于这些政策在执行层面的落地。

Old habits are hard to break. The users you might be used to designing for today—the ones you are used to getting feedback from—might not be representative of all the users you need to reach. We see this play out frequently across all kinds of products, from wearables that do not work for women’s bodies to video-conferencing software that does not work well for people with darker skin tones. So, what’s the way out?

旧习惯难改。你今天习惯为之设计的用户——你习惯从他们那里获得反馈的人——可能并不代表你需要触达的所有用户。我们在各种产品上频繁看到这种情况：从不适配女性身体的可穿戴设备，到对深色肤色人群效果不佳的视频会议软件。那么，出路在哪？

原书第 105 页

  • Take a hard look in the mirror. At Google, we have the brand slogan, “Build For Everyone.” How can we build for everyone when we do not have a representative workforce or engagement model that centralizes community feedback first? We can’t. The truth is that we have at times very publicly failed to protect our most vulnerable users from racist, antisemitic, and homophobic content.

    认真照照镜子。在 Google，我们的品牌口号是“为每个人而建”。如果我们没有一支有代表性的员工队伍、或一种把社区反馈放在首位的互动模式，我们怎么可能为每个人而建？我们做不到。事实是，我们有时非常公开地未能保护最脆弱的用户，使其免受种族主义、反犹太主义和恐同内容的伤害。

  • Don’t build for everyone. Build with everyone. We are not building for everyone yet. That work does not happen in a vacuum, and it certainly doesn’t happen when the technology is still not representative of the population as a whole. That said, we can’t pack up and go home. So how do we build for everyone? We build with our users. We need to engage our users across the spectrum of humanity and be intentional about putting the most vulnerable communities at the center of our design. They should not be an afterthought.

    不要“为”每个人而建，要“与”每个人一起建。我们还没有在为每个人而建。那件事不会在真空中发生，当技术仍不能代表整个人口时就更不会发生。话虽如此，我们不能就此收工回家。那我们如何为每个人而建？我们与用户一起建。我们需要让光谱上所有人的用户都参与进来，并刻意把最脆弱的社群放在我们设计的中心。他们不应当是事后才想起的补丁。

  • Design for the user who will have the most difficulty using your product. Building for those with additional challenges will make the product better for everyone. Another way of thinking about this is: don’t trade equity for short-term velocity.

    为那个使用你产品最困难的用户而设计。为那些面临额外挑战的人而建，会让产品对所有人都更好。另一种思考方式是：不要用公平去换短期速度。

  • Don’t assume equity; measure equity throughout your systems. Recognize that decision makers are also subject to bias and might be undereducated about the causes of inequity. You might not have the expertise to identify or measure the scope of an equity issue. Catering to a single userbase might mean disenfranchising another; these trade-offs can be difficult to spot and impossible to reverse. Partner with individuals or teams that are subject matter experts in diversity, equity, and inclusion.

    不要假定公平；要在你的整个系统中度量公平。要认识到决策者同样受偏见影响、可能对不公的成因所知不足。你也许没有识别或度量一个公平问题范围的专长。迎合单一用户群可能意味着剥夺另一个用户群的权利；这些权衡可能难以察觉、且不可逆转。与多元、公平、包容方面的主题专家或团队合作。

  • Change is possible. The problems we’re facing with technology today, from surveillance to disinformation to online harassment, are genuinely overwhelming. We can’t solve these with the failed approaches of the past or with just the skills we already have. We need to change.

    改变是可能的。我们今天在技术上面临的问题——从监控到虚假信息再到网络骚扰——确实令人不知所措。我们无法用过去失败的方法、或仅凭已有的技能来解决它们。我们需要改变。

Stay Curious, Push Forward · 保持好奇，向前推进

The path to equity is long and complex. However, we can and should transition from simply building tools and services to growing our understanding of how the products we engineer impact humanity. Challenging our education, influencing our teams and managers, and doing more comprehensive user research are all ways to make progress. Although change is uncomfortable and the path to high performance can be painful, it is possible through collaboration and creativity. Lastly, as future exceptional engineers, we should focus first on the users most impacted by bias and discrimination. Together, we can work to accelerate progress by focusing on Continuous Improvement and owning our failures. Becoming an engineer is an involved and continual process. The goal is to make changes that push humanity forward without further disenfranchising the disadvantaged. As future exceptional engineers, we have faith that we can prevent future failures in the system.

通往公平的道路漫长而复杂。然而，我们能够、也应当从“单纯地建造工具与服务”，转向不断加深对“我们所造产品如何影响人类”的理解。挑战我们自己的受教育状况、影响我们的团队与经理、做更全面的用户研究，都是取得进展的方式。尽管改变令人不适、通往高绩效的道路可能痛苦，但通过协作与创造力，它是可能的。最后，作为未来的杰出工程师，我们应当首先聚焦于受偏见与歧视影响最深的用户。通过聚焦持续改进、直面我们的失败，我们共同努力加速进步。成为一名工程师是一个牵涉甚广、持续不断的过程。目标是做出推动人类前进的改变，而不再进一步剥夺弱势群体的权利。作为未来的杰出工程师，我们相信自己能够防止系统中未来的失败。

原书第 106 页

Conclusion · 结语

Developing software, and developing a software organization, is a team effort. As a software organization scales, it must respond and adequately design for its user base, which in the interconnected world of computing today involves everyone, locally and around the world. More effort must be made to make both the development teams that design software and the products that they produce reflect the values of such a diverse and encompassing set of users. And, if an engineering organization wants to scale, it cannot ignore underrepresented groups; not only do such engineers from these groups augment the organization itself, they provide unique and necessary perspectives for the design and implementation of software that is truly useful to the world at large.

开发软件，以及发展一个软件组织，是一项团队事业。随着一个软件组织扩展，它必须做出响应、为其用户群恰当地做设计——在当今互联互通的计算世界里，这个用户群涵盖本地乃至全球的每一个人。必须付出更多努力，让设计软件的开发团队、以及他们所产出的产品，都反映如此多元而包罗万象的用户群的价值观。而且，如果一个工程组织想要扩展，它就不能忽视代表性不足的群体；来自这些群体的工程师不仅充实组织本身，还为设计与实现真正对整个世界有用的软件，提供独特而必要的视角。

TL;DRs · 要点小结（TL;DR）

  • Bias is the default.

    偏见是默认状态。

  • Diversity is necessary to design properly for a comprehensive user base.

    要为全面的用户群恰当做设计，多样性是必要的。

  • Inclusivity is critical not just to improving the hiring pipeline for underrepresented groups, but to providing a truly supportive work environment for all people.

    包容性之所以关键，不仅在于改善代表性不足群体的招聘管道，更在于为所有人提供一个真正有支持性的工作环境。

  • Product velocity must be evaluated against providing a product that is truly useful to all users. It’s better to slow down than to release a product that might cause harm to some users.

    产品速度必须对照“提供一个对所有用户真正有用的产品”来评估。慢下来，也好过发布一个可能伤害某些用户的产品。
